To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the presence of nonspecific binding and ligand depletion in equilibrium binding data can complicate characterizing low affinity sites, (ii) the ratio of low and high affinity binding constants is more robust than individual estimates, and (iii) the presence of a second site can be detected in competition data with a heterologous competitive antagonist.

ligand depletion can be helpful in identifying the low affinity binding site of epibatidiine to α4βnAChR, and that nonspecific binding of [3h]epibatidiine can be a problem when fitting competitive binding data to a two site model, but that it can be distinguished from low-affinity specific epibatidiene binding by measuring nonspecific binding in the absence of α4βnACR.
